plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to meet concentration limits and reduce risk.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
Sell high-beta names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to reduce overall portfolio risk.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and a large cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta exposure, aiming for lower drawdown. Expect modest returns with reduced volatility.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet concentration limits.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to small positions.
Introduce a new position in ERY, a strong scanner setup, for growth.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate returns with controlled risk.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet concentration limits.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU).
Initiate a new position in ERY, a strong scanner setup, with a larger allocation.
This plan aggressively leans into leverage and concentration for stretched growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases leverage and concentration in high-scoring setups. Be aware this raises both upside and drawdown potential, and leveraged ETFs decay daily. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage substantial potential losses.

plan: Add to QQQI, increasing income exposure to 30%.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Sell all high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to near zero.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on yield and capital preservation. It rotates heavily into income ETFs and broad index, cutting leverage and high-beta names. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall; this is not a savings account.
